application_guidance.input_pattern: Composite finite sum with convex uniformly smooth components, strongly convex proximal term, exact indexed gradients and tractable exact prox.
read_original_when: Changing geometry, sampling, output, strong-convexity placement or prox accuracy.
Using Option II, sparse implementations, mini-batches or nonuniform smoothness.
Needing explicit numerical constants or independently establishing the classical inequality imported by Lemma 2.4.
sensitive_conditions: Strong convexity is required of psi; do not substitute strong convexity only of F.
Fresh uniform sampling, exact snapshot full gradient and exact proximal steps.
Geometric snapshot weighting and matched momentum/step parameters.
Memory-dependent gradient counts and separately charged proximal arithmetic.

complexity_scope.guarantee: For every fixed admissible instance and x0, expectation over sampled component indices.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The source uses numerical O prefactors in Theorem 2.1 and equations (2.4)–(2.5); the mapped proof introduces no dependence on n,d,L,sigma,S or Delta0 into those prefactors. No numerical prefactor specified here. Gradient counts exclude proximal-solve arithmetic.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact indexed component gradients, exact full snapshot gradient assembled from n calls each epoch, and exact proximal minimizations of psi at scales alpha and 1/(3L). Fresh uniform index per inner iteration.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Geometrically weighted final snapshot tilde_x^S; E[F(tilde_x^S)]-F(x*). No last-query or last-y guarantee.
complexity_scope.regime: Euclidean; every component convex and uniformly L-smooth; psi sigma-strongly convex; positive n,d,L,sigma. Split at m*sigma/L=3/4, equality in first case. Accuracy complexity uses 0<epsilon<Delta0 in the asymptotic logarithmic regime.
complexity_scope.resource: T=Sm inner iterations; S(n+m) component gradients cached or S(n+2m) uncached, with m=2n. Two exact proximal calls per inner iteration, with psi-dependent solve cost; O(d) dense vector arithmetic per iteration. Snapshot cache O(nd) in general, versus O(d) work-vector memory without cache.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper performance witnessed by Algorithm 1 Option I; no lower bound, support-based class restriction or unrestricted Oracle Complexity optimality extracted.

map: p.10 Lemma 2.3: exact y proximal minimization, smoothness and Young's inequality give F(x)-E F(y_next)>=E Prog(x)-(1/(4L))E||v-grad f(x)||^2.

p.11 Lemma 2.4: apply the displayed convex L-smooth component inequality to gradient differences, average over uniform i and subtract the squared mean. This bounds variance by 2L times the snapshot Bregman gap. The source cites Nesterov (2004), Theorem 2.1.5 for the classical component inequality; that external book was not independently read.
pp.11–12 Lemma 2.5: exact z optimality and sigma-strong convexity of psi yield the proximal mirror three-point inequality, with terminal coefficient (1+alpha*sigma)/2.
pp.12–13 Lemma 2.6: introduce v_point=tau1*z_next+tau2*snapshot+(1-tau1-tau2)*y; combine Lemmas 2.3–2.5 using alpha*tau1<=1/(3L), tau2=1/2, convexity of psi and estimator unbiasedness.
p.13 Lemma 2.7: convexity of f and the three-point x identity cancel the snapshot-gradient inner product; choose u=x* to obtain the one-step objective-gap/z-distance potential inequality.
p.14 Section 2.2: define D_k=F(y_k)-F*, tilde_D^s=F(snapshot^s)-F*, theta=1+alpha*sigma. Multiply by theta^j and sum over the epoch; convexity at the weighted snapshot yields equation (2.3).

pp.14–15 Case 1: for m*sigma/L<=3/4, alpha=1/sqrt(3m*sigma*L), tau1=m*alpha*sigma and alpha*sigma<=1/(2m). The source bounds tau2*(theta^(m-1)-1)+(1-1/theta)<=tau1, obtains theta^(-m) epoch contraction, telescopes, and bounds initial squared distance using strong convexity to obtain (2.4).

p.15 Case 2: for m*sigma/L>3/4, tau1=tau2=1/2 and alpha=2/(3L); theta^m>=1+2*sigma*m/(3L)>=3/2. Equation (2.3) yields contraction by 2/3 per epoch of the snapshot-gap/z-distance potential. Telescoping and strong convexity give (2.5). Combining cases proves the source theorem; Remark 2.2 and footnote 11 supply separate amortized gradient accounting.

assumptions: For every i, f_i:R^d->R is convex and differentiable, and ||grad f_i(x)-grad f_i(y)||<=L||x-y|| for every x,y.
psi is convex, lower semicontinuous, possibly nondifferentiable and sigma-strongly convex: psi(y)>=psi(x)+<g,y-x>+(sigma/2)||y-x||^2 for relevant subgradients g and all x,y.
A minimizer exists; F(x0) is finite; all required exact indexed gradients and proximal minimizations are available.
Use Algorithm 1's parameters, Option I y update and geometric snapshot output; known L and sigma are valid bounds.
statement.conclusion: E[F(tilde_x^S)]-F(x*)<=O((1+sqrt(sigma/(3Lm)))^(-Sm))*Delta0 when m*sigma/L<=3/4, and <=O(1.5^(-S))*Delta0 when m*sigma/L>3/4. Theorem 2.1 states that for m=Theta(n), including m=2n here, expected gap <=epsilon is achieved in O((n+sqrt(nL/sigma))*log(Delta0/epsilon)) inner iterations. Remark 2.2 and footnote 11 give the same asymptotic component-gradient count: 1.5 amortized per iteration with all snapshot gradients stored, or 2.5 without storage. Option I additionally uses two exact proximal evaluations per inner iteration.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For positive integers n,d, on Euclidean R^d define f=(1/n)sum_{i=1}^n f_i and F=f+psi. Choose x* in argmin F and x0 with finite Delta0=F(x0)-F(x*). Run Algorithm 1 Option I as specified in alg.P021.katyusha_sc: m=2n, tau2=1/2, tau1=min{sqrt(m*sigma/(3L)),1/2}, alpha=1/(3*tau1*L), y0=z0=tilde_x^0=x0, exact snapshot full gradients, uniform indexed control variates, two exact proximal updates and snapshot weights (1+alpha*sigma)^j. Output tilde_x^S.
statement.parameter_domains: n,d>=1 integers; L,sigma>0; m=2n; S>=0 integer. For the accuracy consequence Delta0>0 and 0<epsilon<Delta0. The displayed logarithmic complexity is asymptotic in accuracy, in particular log(Delta0/epsilon)>=1; near epsilon=Delta0 retain integer-epoch/constant overhead. If Delta0=0 the gap bound is zero.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed admissible instance and initial x0, and every nonnegative integer S, the bound holds in expectation over all freshly uniform component indices conditional on preceding history. This is expected primal objective error, not a pathwise or high-probability statement.
